title: Student Riots in India, Albania and France Show 'USAID' Effect Still Around - Whatfinger News Quick Hits
text:
Some people like to argue that the wave of right-wing candidates winning elections in Latin America is due to the shutdown of USAID.
I wouldn’t celebrate just yet.
We’re currently watching ‘student riots’ in France, Albania and India. And those don’t just happen on their own.
Remember that USAID was just one component in a worldwide leftist machine that has been running now for generations. It’s built up organizations worldwide, trained staff and pumped endless millions into various non-profits around the world… many of which are still operating. Part of that machine was funded by massively wealthy foundations like those of Ford and Soros. Losing USAID was a blow, but the machine is still operating. And we weren’t the only government funding it. The Euros were putting money in the NGO machine.
And at least some of these groups also have ties to enemy nations including China, Russia and Iran who are more than happy to benefit from their political sabotage.
Back to the riots. Of the three riots, the most crucial are the ones in India where the Left hopes to topple Modi. Losing India would be a major blow, and a Leftist-Islamic government heading up a major country would be a major threat. Macron in France, much less so, but the riots there are, as they often are with leftists, an attempt at political mobilization of the ‘youth’ and ‘minorities’.
The Albania riots are more of an exception to the usual rule since the target is a leftist leader linked to the Soros clan. But there may be a complicated interplay of interests there.
Either way, the leftist student riots around the world aren’t a coincidence, they’re a strategy.
